analysis.title: AI Exports, Copper, and France - GS Daily Monitor
key_insights: The Trump Administration issued an interim chip export rule requiring data center operators in certain countries to obtain a US government license before exporting AI chips from NVDA and other US manufacturers.
Market attention is on AI and NVDA's EPS after the close on 17 Nov 2026. US equities were choppy in the morning.
The Shanghai Futures Exchange stepped in to ease a historic copper squeeze by pressing long and short positions to settle financially rather than through physical delivery.
An aluminum supply squeeze is intensifying, with the Tom/next spread jumping more than $15 a ton.

French bonds sold off across the curve after Le Pen's discussions on pension reforms. Her proposal included lowering the retirement age to as low as 60 and adding an individually funded pension pillar.
Taiex fell as much as 3.1% early Tuesday on AI chip curb headlines and forced retail liquidation.
The PBOC delivered a 254bn net liquidity injection, with credit bonds stabilizing and redemption pressure easing.
A Kremlin aide said the trilateral Putin-Xi-Trump meeting later this week should have great influence on development of the international situation.
Lebanese banks escalated their dispute with the government over the proposed taxation of unrealized gains and provisions against defaulted Eurobonds.

Chart of the Day: US copper inventory has built up this year as the metal continues to leave Shanghai. Recent headlines focus on the SHFE's reported intervention to encourage financial settlement over physical delivery.
earnings_insights: NVDA reports EPS after the close on 17 Nov 2026. The note gives no estimate or figure.
